sources.title: CAGI, the Critical Assessment of Genome Interpretation, establishes progress and prospects for computational genetic variant interpretation methods
authors: The Critical Assessment of Genome Interpretation Consortium
sources.summary: The Critical Assessment of Genome Interpretation (CAGI) aims to advance the state of the art for computational prediction of genetic variant impact, particularly those relevant to disease. The five complete editions of the CAGI community experiment comprised 50 challenges, in which participants made blind predictions of phenotypes from genetic data, and these were evaluated by independent assessors. Overall, results show that while current methods are imperfect, they have major utility for research and clinical applications. sources.title: Deep neural network improves the estimation of polygenic risk scores for breast cancer
sources.summary: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) estimate the genetic risk of an individual for a complex disease based on many genetic variants across the whole genome. In this study, we compared a series of computational models for estimation of breast cancer PRS. A deep neural network (DNN) was found to outperform alternative machine learning techniques and established statistical algorithms, including BLUP, BayesA and LDpred. sources.title: CRISPR Genome Engineering for Human Pluripotent Stem Cell Research
sources.summary: The emergence of targeted and efficient genome editing technologies, such as repurposed bacterial programmable nucleases (e.g., CRISPR-Cas systems), has abetted the development of cell engineering approaches. Lessons learned from the development of RNA-interference (RNA-i) therapies can spur the translation of genome editing, such as those enabling the translation of human pluripotent stem cell engineering. sources.title: Childhood Trauma in Schizophrenia: Current Findings and Research Perspectives
sources.summary: Schizophrenia is a severe neuropsychiatric disorder with persistence of symptoms throughout adult life in most of the affected patients. This unfavorable course is associated with multiple episodes and residual symptoms, mainly negative symptoms and cognitive deficits. The neural diathesis-stress model proposes that psychosocial stress acts on a pre-existing vulnerability and thus triggers the symptoms of schizophrenia. sources.title: Mitochondrial Genomics in Relation to Neuroimaging and Oxygen Dynamics in Youth Bipolar Disorder
sources.summary: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a severe psychiatric disorder affecting approximately 1-3% of youth. Mitochondrial dysfunction is implicated in the neuropathology of BD. Higher circulating cell-free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) and mitochondrial DNA variants, linked to poor mitochondrial health, are associated with BD risk, symptom severity, altered treatment response, and protein dysfunction.
